content.value_statement: Seed data projects face complex germplasm, ownership, important-data, and approval requirements. This skill structures assessments and assetization plans before valuation or RWA work begins.
actual_capabilities: Classifies breeding, genomic, weather, soil, machinery, and traceability data by asset characteristics.
Checks germplasm, variety approval, genetically modified organism, and important-data compliance gates.
Maps contributions, rights, authorizations, and benefit allocation across farmers, cooperatives, platforms, and breeders.
Designs data aggregation, quality, lineage, desensitization, registration, and delivery workflows.
Structures valuation and RWA planning for eligible varieties, datasets, and data income rights.
Produces assessment tables, compliance checklists, ownership plans, SOPs, and quality controls.
limitations: Does not grant variety approval, germplasm approval, or other administrative authorization.
Does not replace licensed appraisers, lawyers, financial institutions, or data exchanges.
Policy references require verification against current regulator publications and local rules.
Cannot determine ownership or value without project evidence, contracts, data inventories, and approval records.

use_cases.title: Screen Cooperative Data
use_cases.description: Classify farm and breeding datasets, identify missing authorizations, and determine whether assetization can proceed.

use_cases.title: Plan Breeding Data Registration
use_cases.description: Separate variety rights from data rights and prepare a registration and valuation work plan.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agricultural RWA Readiness
use_cases.description: Review compliance gates, ownership evidence, important-data exposure, and proposed income-right structures.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Seed Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these datasets as breeding, genomic, weather, soil, machinery, or traceability data. Explain each asset characteristic and required evidence: [dataset inventory].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner classification of a data inventory

prompt_templates.title: Run a Compliance Screening
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this project for germplasm, variety approval, genetically modified organism, important-data, personal-information, and cross-border concerns: [project details]. Return proceed, remediate, or stop.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Ownership Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Map data contributions and rights for farmers, cooperatives, platforms, and breeders. Propose required authorizations, benefit allocation, evidence, and unresolved decisions: [stakeholders and contracts].

prompt_templates.title: Build an Assetization and RWA Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased roadmap from compliance review through data processing, registration, valuation, and RWA assessment. Include deliverables, dependencies, stop conditions, quality checks, and responsible parties: [project dossier].

output_examples.input: A cooperative provides soil, field location, machinery, and harvest records collected from 300 farms.
output: Main gaps: farmer authorization, platform processing rights, location-data classification, and documented lineage.
Next deliverables: data inventory, authorization matrix, important-data assessment, and aggregation plan.

output_examples.input: A breeder wants to tokenize germplasm samples and genomic records for international investors.
output: Status: stop the proposed structure pending formal review.
Germplasm and genomic data may face strict provision, exchange, biosafety, and cross-border controls.
Assess approved variety rights and eligible domestic data income rights as separate alternatives.

output_examples.input: A seed company has approved varieties, trial data, signed contributor agreements, and five years of licensing income.
output: Status: potentially suitable for detailed valuation and RWA assessment.
Verify agreement scope, data rights, dataset quality, income attribution, and important-data boundaries.
Use documented income assumptions and sensitivity analysis before selecting a financing structure.

best_practices: Provide a complete data inventory, stakeholder map, contracts, approvals, processing history, and intended use.
Verify current laws, regulator guidance, and local registration rules before relying on any recommendation.
Treat compliance gates and written authorization as prerequisites for valuation, registration, financing, or RWA planning.
anti_patterns: Do not treat germplasm, variety rights, and data rights as the same legal asset.
Do not estimate value or promote financing without evidence, assumptions, and sensitivity analysis.
Do not share precise agricultural locations, genomic data, or personal information before classification and authorization.

faq.question: What data types can this skill assess?
faq.answer: It covers breeding, genomic, weather, soil, machinery, production, and traceability data used in seed industry projects.

faq.question: Can it approve a germplasm or variety project?
faq.answer: No. It identifies likely requirements, but competent agricultural authorities issue approvals and registrations.

faq.question: Does it provide a formal valuation?
faq.answer: No. It can structure valuation inputs and methods, but a qualified appraiser must issue any required formal report.

faq.question: How does it handle multi-party ownership?
faq.answer: It maps contributions, contractual rights, processing roles, authorizations, and benefit allocation for each participating party.

faq.question: Can all seed industry data support RWA financing?
faq.answer: No. Eligibility depends on lawful sources, clear rights, approvals, data classification, reliable income, and the proposed structure.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the dataset inventory, stakeholders, contracts, approvals, geographic scope, processing history, intended users, and financing objective.
